content.text: Found it — this is the classic flexbox overflow bug. The scroll container at [AnnotationTimeline.tsx:343](frontend/src/components/annotate/AnnotationTimeline.tsx:343) is `flex: 1` with `overflowX: 'auto'`, but flex items default to `min-width: auto`, so once the inner content (`width: W`) grows past the available space at higher zoom, the flex item refuses to shrink and instead pushes the whole row (and the page) wider instead of scrolling internally. Adding `minWidth: 0` lets it shrink and confines the scrollbar to the timeline.

content.text:
That's the final state. Fixed and verified in the browser (zoomed all the way to 12x with no page-level horizontal scroll).

**Root cause:** two nested flexbox containers were sized by their content instead of shrinking to fit:
1. [AnnotationTimeline.tsx:343](frontend/src/components/annotate/AnnotationTimeline.tsx:343) — the scrollable timeline track is a `flex: 1` item, but flex items default to `min-width: auto`, so once the zoomed-in content got wider than the available space, it refused to shrink and pushed its flex row wider instead of scrolling internally.
2. [Annotate.tsx:481](frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx:481) — the page's content wrapper uses `margin: '0 auto'` to center itself inside a column-flex layout. Auto margins on a flex item switch it to content-based (shrink-to-fit) sizing instead of stretching to the parent's width, so it also grew to accommodate the wide timeline, up to its `maxWidth: 1560`.

Both needed `min-width: 0` / an explicit `width: 100%` to force them to respect the available viewport width and let the timeline's own `overflowX: auto` contain the scrollbar.
